selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: current cron config, users, and service state before changes
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed no cron.allow/cron.deny existed, cron service active, opsadmin user absent, root present

selected_evidence.requirement: Restrict cron scheduling to root and opsadmin only
selected_evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.allow with exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', removed any cron.deny

selected_evidence.requirement: Prove non-listed users are denied cron scheduling
selected_evidence.summary: testdeny user's crontab install attempt failed with 'cannot use this program (crontab)', exit=1

selected_evidence.requirement: Prove root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs
selected_evidence.summary: Both root and opsadmin successfully installed and listed a crontab entry, exit=0
Removed test crontabs, deleted testdeny and testuser2 accounts

selected_evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restart (boot identity + cron config/service state)
selected_evidence.summary: cron.allow contains root/opsadmin, no cron.deny, cron service active/enabled, pre-restart boot_id bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49 captured
Backgrounded systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' before node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart causes disconnection then reconnection with changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Connection reset confirms node down; subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id ec37444a-5558-4aff-a094-c4b4ff85cf49, differing from pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron access control and enforcement
selected_evidence.summary: After restart: /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, no cron.deny, cron service active/enabled, opsadmin user intact, root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs, and user 'nobody' is denied access
